findings.F1: Over all up days in every profile, the next-day excess return falls as the close sits deeper below the 20-day high. The deepest depth quintile is followed by -1.09 % (706 cases, t -5.0); the other quintiles give -0.08 %, -0.34 %, -0.10 % and +0.26 %. The slope of e on depth has a t of +2.08, clustered by day (3527 cases, 889 days), and a positive slope here means deeper closes are followed by larger falls.
findings.F2: The deepest up-day quintile's fade is not confined to one coin, but it weakens over time. Five of six coins give between -1.09 % and -1.38 % with t from -2.2 to -2.8 (XRP: -0.26 %, t -0.4). By year it is negative in 2018, 2019 and 2020 (-1.76 %, -0.73 %, -1.58 %) and near zero in 2021 (-0.04 %).
findings.F3: Inside the tested profile, falling agitated, the effect is not graded. The slope t is 0.12 (361 cases, 126 days). The depth quintiles give -1.71 %, -0.32 %, -2.00 %, -0.42 % and -0.44 %, and the book's own depth quartiles give -1.10 %, -0.19 %, -1.41 % and -0.73 %. Only the level of the fade is there (mean -1.05 %, t -2.08), which explains the inconclusive verdict.
findings.F4: In falling calm markets the up-day fade is cleanly graded. Its depth quintiles run -1.01 %, -0.01 %, -0.08 %, +0.48 % and +0.69 % from deepest to shallowest (541 cases, 220 days). The slope t is 1.45 on its own, and this is the profile the tested idea excluded.
findings.F5: In choppy markets a close deep below the 20-day high is followed by a further fall, whichever way the day closed. The deepest quintile gives -1.75 % after up days (58 cases) and -1.99 % after down days (54 cases). For down days the quintiles climb steadily to +0.86 % at the shallowest. The cases are few, with slope t 1.19 for up days and 1.13 for down days.
findings.F6: Down days that close nearest their 20-day high are followed by a next-day rise of +0.70 % (685 cases, t 3.5). The rise is graded across the quintiles (+0.09 % to +0.70 %), but the day-clustered slope t is only 0.95 and the effect does not hold by year (only 2020 has t 2.2). It is close to the nearness-to-high continuation ideas the map already holds.
findings.F7: Other angles look either already held or like chance, given how many angles were checked:

ideas.idea: When a coin closes up on the day, the further that close sits below its 20-day high, measured in units of its 20-day daily swing, the larger its fall over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader fades up days that close deep below the recent high in any market, with a larger short the deeper the close, rather than only in falling agitated markets where the grading is absent.
ideas.name: deep up day fade everywhere

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, when a coin closes up on the day, the further that close sits below its 20-day high, measured in units of its 20-day daily swing, the larger its fall over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts deep-below-high up days in calm declines, sized by the depth, which fills the thinly held falling-calm short box.
ideas.name: calm fall up day fade

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the further a coin's close sits below its 20-day high, measured in units of its 20-day daily swing, the larger its fall over the next day, whether the day itself closed up or down.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a sideways market shorts coins pressed deep below their recent high, which is a breakdown continuation in the empty choppy short boxes, not a rebound.
ideas.name: choppy deep close continuation
